Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-15
Start: 15:00 BST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Dr. Laura Chen (Pinegrove Head of ML), Miguel Santos (Infra Lead), Anya Petrov (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in focused on capacity uplift, EU edge activation timeline, and contract extension options. Customer seeks lower P95 latency in EU, data residency assurances, and a predictable monthly commitment with burst capacity. Redwood AE/SE to provide revised pricing, benchmark plan, and technical ops playbook.

Topics:
- Current usage and forecast
- EU edge private tenancy / VPC options
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs (dedicated vs hosted)
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO)
- Next steps and dates for procurement

Action items (short):
- Quote, SOC2 docs, benchmark plan, usage numbers, contract redlines

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, can you hear me okay?
[00:12] Laura: Yeah I can hear you, thanks. Sorry we had a back-to-back earlier, so we'll be a bit tight on time.
[00:20] Jordan: No problem, we'll try to be concise. Priya and I wanted to run through the renewal options and the EU edge activation plan. We're penciled for an 18-month extension? I think that's what Miguel requested, right?
[00:32] Miguel: Yeah, our ops team prefers an 18 month commit, minimizes churn for capacity planning, and then we need EU residency for model logs.
[00:40] Priya: Cool. Quick question though, Miguel — are you expecting to go fully private (on-prem/VPC) for the EU edge or a Redwood-managed EU region with private tenancy?
[00:52] Miguel: Initially Redwood-managed EU region with private tenancy. On-prem is, uh, heavier for us, compliance might push it later but not right now.
[01:05] Laura: From ML side we care about the P95 tail for generation — some of our clinical inference requests can't tolerate more than 230ms in EU. So the latency targets matter.
[01:18] Jordan: Understood. We have two levers — Dedicated capacity pinned to your account in eu-west, or hosted with burst and routing policies to keep latency down. Dedicated gives the best deterministic tail but costs more.
[01:31] Miguel: How much more? at a ballpark.
[01:34] Priya: Ballpark on our last similar deal — dedicated was roughly 30-40% higher for the steady-state commit but gave consistent P95 improvements of ~40-60ms depending on model and seq length. If you pair that with prefix caching and tuned batching we can hit the 230ms target more reliably.
[01:52] Laura: Are those numbers with KV cache enabled? We have long conversation threads and a fair amount of reused context.
[01:58] Priya: Yes, cache on. For your workload the KV cache hit-rate will significantly cut per-token compute. We'll validate it in the benchmark.
[02:10] Anya: On procurement, two asks — pricing schedule and the data residency wording. We need to show this to legal. Also any SSO/SAML integration docs.
[02:20] Jordan: We'll send a revised quote showing two options: hosted + EU add-on with burst, and dedicated EU pool with burst. We'll include sample monthly costs and a delta view.
[02:31] Miguel: Also curious about key management — can Redwood integrate with our KMS? We can't have key material leave our control for logs at least.
[02:40] Priya: Yes, we've got customer-managed keys support in private deployments and a bring-your-own-key option for certain hosted plans. We'll attach the KMS integration guide; there are a couple of caveats around HSM-backed signing and rotation.
[02:55] Laura: Also audit logs retention — we need 7 years for certain tracing. Can you do longer retention or export hooks?
[03:04] Jordan: We can extend retention as part of the enterprise package or provide a log export to your SIEM. We'll surface options in the docs.
[03:15] Miguel: Ok thanks. Can we talk about the activation timeline? We want EU edge live before product freeze on 2025-10-01.
[03:24] Priya: For a Redwood-managed EU private tenancy with reserved capacity, typical lead time is 4–6 weeks after the PO and final config. If you want additional private tenancy isolation we might add 1–2 weeks.
[03:37] Jordan: So if procurement signs by early September we should be OK for an early October activation, assuming no legal holdups.
[03:45] Anya: That seems tight but possible. We'll try to push.
[03:48] Laura: One more technical — we've had tokenization differences across models, does Redwood provide a stable tokenizer mapping or is that per model variant?
[03:58] Priya: Tokenization is model-specific. That said we expose consistent pre- and post-processing hooks and you can pin model versions. We'll add recommended tokenizer configs for your inference path.
[04:12] Miguel: For the benchmark — what do you need from us? QPS, peak tokens, sample payloads?
[04:18] Priya: Exactly — sample payloads, representative QPS/peak tokens/day, example prompt distributions. If you can give us a 48-hour sample we can run an apples-to-apples throughput and tail latency benchmark.
[04:30] Laura: We can pull a week of anonymized logs but I'll need sign-off. Is anonymized data enough for the perf bench?
[04:36] Priya: Yes, anonymized is fine, as long as tokenization is representative. We mostly need sequence length distribution and concurrency characteristics.
[04:45] Jordan: We'll plan to run a benchmark week of 2025-08-25 — we'll schedule with Miguel and run it in Redwood staging with your sample traffic.
[04:55] Miguel: One concern — fallback policy. If eu-west experiences capacity exhaustion can requests spill to another region? We want predictable behavior for EU-only PII flows.
[05:06] Priya: We can configure strict routing by policy — you can prevent cross-region fallback for sensitive routes, or allow best-effort fallback to low-latency compatible variants. We'll document both approaches and recommended failover playbooks.
[05:20] Jordan: On the pricing model — if you commit to 18 months with a modest uplift we can include a burst pool and a reduced per-token rate for embedding workloads. We'll show line items.
[05:31] Anya: Do you have standard redlines in your contracts for data residency? We need the clause language to present to legal.
[05:38] Jordan: We'll attach a sample amendment with residency and audit clauses that you can insert.
[05:44] Laura: Are there any performance regressions you track when you flip quantization or compression settings? We can't degrade accuracy too much.
[05:53] Priya: Good point — our Optimize team maintains quality baselines. For quantization profiles we provide recommended configs per model and run evals on your prompt set to ensure quality regressions are within agreed thresholds. We'll include the QA report template.
[06:08] Miguel: Ok. On the KMS front, one technical ask — do you produce server-side encrypted logs so we can verify key wrapping?
[06:15] Priya: Yes, logs can be encrypted server-side with your key and we can provide key-wrapping proof artifacts.
[06:22] Jordan: Alright to recap: Redwood to send revised quote with two options, include SOC2/ISO and KMS docs, propose a benchmark week (week of 8/25), and attach sample residency amendment. Customer to provide usage samples, QPS and legal redlines.
[06:36] Anya: Correct. Procurement will try to get sign-off by 9/5 but we can't promise. I'll escalate.
[06:42] Miguel: One small question — what about support SLAs during the pilot? We need at least 4-hour response for severity 1 during activation.
[06:50] Jordan: We can include a time-limited activation SLA in the contract addendum for the onboarding phase; after live we can map to enterprise SLA tiers.
[06:59] Laura: Great. Also curious about observability — do you provide per-route token-level cost breakdowns? That was useful previously.
[07:07] Priya: Yes, Console exposes per-route cost + latency breakdowns, plus trace hooks. We'll include screenshots in the ops playbook.
[07:16] Speaker 6: (inaudible) can you share the benchmark plan link?
[07:20] Jordan: We'll post the benchmark template and a shared folder after this call.
[07:25] Laura: Alright thanks.
[07:28] Jordan: Anything else from your side?
[07:31] Miguel: Not for now. We'll collate QPS and sample payloads and aim to have them by 8/18.
[07:38] Anya: I'll try to get legal's initial read by 8/22, but redlines might slip to end of month.
[07:45] Jordan: Good. We'll follow up with the quote and docs by 8/20 and schedule the bench.
[07:50] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[07:52] Laura: Thanks all.
